scenes.0: Same robot. Same task. One run succeeds, one fails. Move the can three centimeters, and it misses. So which build do you ship, and what still blocks deployment?
scenes.1: [[pause:0.3]] Quant Gate answers three questions. [[pause:0.2]] Which candidate do I validate first? Can this build deploy? And what do I test next?
scenes.2: It started with an arm that brings a drink to someone working hard. This S O one oh one runs an A C T policy on a [Jetson](/dʒˈɛtsən/) [Orin](/ˈɔɹɪn/) Nano Super, trained on [Nebius](/nˈɛbiəs/) Jobs. From that one policy we built twenty-six TensorRT engines: full precision, half precision, and twenty-four [int](/ˈɪnt/) eight calibrations. Seven hundred and forty-five real-arm trials ran from sealed, interleaved schedules.
scenes.3: First decision: what to validate first. Measured on this [Jetson](/dʒˈɛtsən/), half precision was the fastest engine and the cheapest per inference, not [int](/ˈɪnt/) eight.
scenes.4: But cost is not approval. In the nominal tests, every candidate succeeded ninety to a hundred percent of the time, and the offline audit's top picks did no better than random picks. Twenty-five trials cannot tell them apart, so the verdict is: not enough evidence yet.
scenes.5: We detected no success difference between the precisions. The clearest failures came from the physical setup. Without the gripper pads, eight of twenty-four. A start moved three centimeters: missed. Fifty new demonstrations and a sealed comparison: twelve of twelve, against three of twelve. We repeated it for the next gaps, a smaller can and six centimeters out: twelve of twelve in both, against the first fine-tune in the same session.
scenes.6: Even the camera mount is in scope. When success dropped, we kept every result sealed, and traced it to a knocked wrist camera.
scenes.7: Cosmos Reason, on a [Nebius](/nˈɛbiəs/) A I Endpoint, judges the final frame of each trial. On ninety-six new trials, it caught twenty-two of twenty-four failures, with two false alarms in seventy-two. [Nemotron](/nˈimOtɹˌɑn/) Super on Token Factory explains the review, while code writes every number and verdict.
scenes.8: Here is what a developer does with it. Pick a candidate: half precision. The evidence: cost on the device, and results on the arm. The verdict: hold. It is not approved, because the comparison is still too small. The plan says what to run next, under a pre-registered rule. And a build whose files no longer match what was audited is blocked before it reaches the arm.
scenes.9: Validate half precision first. Hold deployment. Run the listed test. [[pause:0.4]] Quant Gate. [[pause:0.3]] Earn the next test, not the approval.
